headline: Russia readies massive missile strike, repositioning bombers for imminent attack
subheadline: Tu-95MS bombers moved from Far East to Engels and Olenya airfields, five more aircraft being armed for a strike by end of next week
lede: IDF carried out simultaneous airstrikes on Nabatieh and Ali Taher in southern Lebanon while launching a snap multi‑front drill testing infiltration, rocket attacks, and Gaza border breaches. Iran’s IRGC claimed to have struck a US Sentinel drone in the Strait of Hormuz, prompting US Central Command to denounce the claim as a ‘pure lie,’ while Tehran declared a new restricted zone. In Ukraine, Russia repositioned Tu‑95MS bombers from the Far East to Engels and Olenya airfields, arming five additional aircraft for a massive missile strike expected by week’s end, as Kyiv destroyed helicopters at Sochi Adler and struck the Ryazan oil refinery. Hezbollah received Iranian approval to withdraw from Ali Taher ridge, and the Kremlin’s advisor Ushakov affirmed Russia will not compromise on war aims despite ongoing negotiations.

sections.title: Russian bombers repositioned for imminent missile strike
sections.body: Russia is repositioning Tu‑95MS strategic bombers from the Far East to Engels and Olenya airfields, arming five additional aircraft for a massive missile strike anticipated by the end of next week. Ukrainian forces struck the Ryazan oil refinery, a key logistics hub processing 17 million tons annually, and destroyed Ka‑52 and Mi‑28 helicopters at Sochi Adler airport, with a Mi‑8 also damaged. Intensive UAV and jet‑drone campaigns hit Odesa, Mykolaiv, Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk regions, including KABs on Kharkiv and Donetsk areas, while enemy advances near Kostiantynivka and UAV threats target multiple settlements. Kremlin advisor Yuri Ushakov confirmed Russia will not compromise on military objectives, citing ‘noticeable successes’ and confidence in achieving stated goals after talks with U.S. envoys.

sections.title: IDF strikes Nabatieh, Ali Taher amid drills
sections.body: IDF conducted simultaneous airstrikes on Nabatieh and Ali Taher in southern Lebanon while issuing alerts for expected attacks across the Lebanon front, including the Valley of Hula and Ramim Ridge. A snap multi‑front drill led by Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir simulated scenarios such as 10‑15 terrorists infiltrating from Lebanon, rocket attacks on Tel Aviv, and Gaza border breaches. Hezbollah received Iranian ‘green light’ to exit the Ali Taher ridge, signaling a potential shift on the Lebanon front, and the IRGC claimed to have targeted a US Sentinel drone in the Strait of Hormuz, a claim US Central Command denied as a ‘pure lie.’ IDF also struck a vehicle in central Gaza, reportedly eliminating a Hamas military wing commander.

sections.title: Intelligence Assessment
sections.body: The convergence of IDF airstrikes, large‑scale multi‑front drills, and Iranian‑US tensions over the Strait of Hormuz indicates an elevated threat environment, while Russia’s bomber repositioning and intensified UAV strikes suggest preparation for a coordinated combined‑arms offensive. Hezbollah’s approved withdrawal from Ali Taher and the Kremlin’s insistence on unchanged war aims reflect strategic recalibrations that could reshape the respective fronts.
